title: Embryo, Cotyledons, Radicle, Hypocotyl, and Plumule
objective: Trace the embryo structures that become the early root and shoot system.

terms.definition: The young sporophyte contained within the seed.
An embryonic leaf that stores or transfers reserves and becomes photosynthetic after emergence.
The embryonic root that normally emerges first during germination.
The embryonic stem region below the cotyledons.
The embryonic shoot region containing the shoot apex and earliest leaf primordia.

coreScience: The cannabis embryo is a compact plant body prepared to resume growth when water, temperature, oxygen, and viability permit. The radicle is the first obvious organ to extend. Its emergence marks germination in many seed-testing definitions. The radicle anchors the seedling and develops into the initial root axis, from which lateral roots and absorbing surfaces expand.

The hypocotyl elongates and helps lift the cotyledons during emergence. The two cotyledons open above the medium, become green, and contribute photosynthesis while the first true leaves expand. Cotyledons are not the first true leaves: they are embryo structures with a simpler shape and a different developmental origin.

The shoot apex between the cotyledons produces the first true leaves and subsequent stem nodes. Radicle injury, constriction around the hypocotyl, persistent seed coverings, or oxygen depletion in saturated media can interrupt emergence. Salinity and disease can also impair establishment, but they require their own measurements and evidence rather than being inferred from a stalled seedling.
cultivationRelevance: Perfect manual orientation is less important than avoiding radicle injury. Roots generally reorient through gravitropism, but handling method, developmental stage, and physical obstruction affect the outcome; long exposed radicles are especially easy to damage.
Score emergence by structure: radicle appearance, cotyledon opening, first true leaves, and normal root-shoot balance. Do not call every emerged seedling healthy.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Date and time from start, plus approximate length if needed.
Upright, stretched, constricted, discolored, or damaged.
Opened, green, damaged, retained covering, or abnormal.
Date visible and symmetry or distortion.
Normal, weak root, weak shoot, or both abnormal.

misconceptions: The first two round leaves are true leaves: They are cotyledons.
The emerging radicle should be green: It is embryonic root tissue and is typically pale before light exposure or abnormal greening.
A seedling that breaks the surface has passed: Normal development requires coordinated roots, hypocotyl, cotyledons, and shoot apex.
evidenceLimits: Exact emergence timing depends on seed lot, temperature, moisture, oxygen, and method. The structural sequence is more transferable than a fixed hour count.
